correctness.rationale: For fixed interior fitness and positive R, conditioning on the last clearing age gives the stationary Poisson-family PGF. Its first immigration derivative is controlled by the integrable clearing age; taking the v-fold product yields the compound-Poisson exponent with finite total intensity ≤a/R. The one-founder mass has geometric ratio x=λ(1−e^(−gt))/(μ−λe^(−gt)), and dx/dt is λ times its positive-state prefactor. An independent limit replay therefore gives Λ_n=(a/λ)∫_0^(λ/μ) x^(n−1)[(λ−μx)/(λ(1−x))]^(R/g) dx. Set μ=1, w=g, u=n(1−x). The support becomes nw≤u≤n; the bracket before exponentiation is (1−nw/u)/(1−w) in [0,1]. Since nR→s and nw→0, its power tends to exp(−s/u) at each u>0; (1−u/n)^(n−1) is bounded by exp(−u/2) for n≥2. The upper-edge density is finite by ν<1 and the β condition, and q tends to zero there, so a/λ→1. Dominated convergence gives nΛ_n→∫_0^∞exp(−u−s/u)du=2√s K_1(2√s), with the stated two endpoint asymptotics of the profile. This proves the ordered limits under the frozen site model, not simultaneous network convergence. CHECK.py was inspected, not executed; its finite experiments are supplementary.

value.rationale: The crossover function determines individual large-clan intensities on the clearing scale, distinguishes the near-log-series and stretched-exponential regimes, and explains which parameters disappear under rescaling. Neither a fixed-fitness tail nor finitely many integrated moment thresholds describes this crossover. The model's independently factorized scope and the ordered limits are essential to this interpretation.
